dedupe_keys.name: multi modal sensor data of canadian critical electrical infrastructure roadside images segmentation labels and lidar carleton university

description: This Borealis dataset from Carleton University is a multi-modal sensor resource for training and evaluating algorithms that monitor electrical critical infrastructure in the Canadian environment. A data acquisition system built from commercially available colour cameras and 3D LiDAR sensors was mounted on a ground vehicle and driven along road corridors in the National Capital Region, recording poles, high-tension wires and transformers with the sensors registered in time and space for fusion. The release holds 440 scenes and 1.77 GB of data; each scene includes an image, semantic segmentation labels with five classes as PNG and NPY files, and the matching LiDAR data. Version 1.1 is available for free download under CC0 and its metadata were updated in November 2025. Coverage is the Ottawa-Gatineau National Capital Region, Canada. Caveats: the scenes are road-corridor views from one region and five label classes, so models may not transfer to other networks without retraining. Simulation uses are automated detection of distribution poles, wires and transformers for asset inventories and digital twins of overhead networks. Related records: data-geooutagekg-florida-power-outage-knowledge-graph is another machine learning resource for grid monitoring.
